newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony to start selling PCs in Japan in July.
newsitem.headline: Sony to start selling PCs in Japan in July.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Tuesday that it will start selling its Vaio series of personal computers for the Japanese market from July 1.
Sony said it will have monthly production capacity of 3,000 units for two models of notebook personal computers and 1,000 units for its mini-tower desktop personal computers.
Sony plans to sell the three products under an open price system, with no suggested retail price.
The company will offer two types of notebook PCs, each equipped with a 166 megahertz or 150 megahertz Pentium chip, with sales scheduled to begin on July 1.
The mini-tower PCs, equipped with a 266 megahertz Pentium chip, will be sold from July 15.
The mini-tower will have a built-in CD-R drive and includes features designed to facilitate video editing and television recording, the company said.
The notebook models are 37.6 millimetres thick and weigh 2.4 kilograms.
